messages:
samir: fyi — customer reported webhook failures right after our overnight NAT maintenance. ticket: https://rwd.support/t/45821 :rotating_light:

maya: which customer? logs or example request?

samir: acme-integration (contacted via our support form). They see 403s from their side for all inbound webhooks starting ~02:12 UTC. I pushed the sample curl they sent:

samir: ```
curl -v -X POST https://hooks.acme.example/ingest \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'User-Agent: RedwoodWebhook/1.2' \n  -d '{"event":"order.created","id":12345}'
```

julia: got the 403 response body from them?

samir: yes, they included: `{"error":"forbidden","msg":"source not allowed"}`

luis: ok that definitely reads like an allowlist on their side blocking our source IP. Did they share what IP they expect?

samir: they said they had allowed `34.125.201.45` in their firewall. Our NAT rotation changed the SNAT to a different address during the window — see bot log below.

egress-rotation-bot: NAT rotation completed: old_eip=34.125.201.45 new_eip=34.125.210.77 pool=prod-vpc-3 window=02:00-02:15 UTC maint_id=mnt-2026-03-17

maya: can we confirm the outbound addr used for those webhook requests? Any traces in our delivery logs?

samir: delivery trace (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T02:13:07Z deliver attempt id=abc123 src=redwood-host-7 dst=https://hooks.acme.example/ingest src_ip=34.125.210.77 status=403
2026-03-17T02:13:36Z deliver attempt id=abc124 src=redwood-host-9 dst=https://hooks.acme.example/ingest src_ip=34.125.210.77 status=403
```

luis: matches the bot. So their allowlist hasn't been updated. We should ask them to add the new_eip or provide a stable egress hostname.

julia: I already pinged the customer with a quick workaround — asked them to temporarily allow 34.125.210.77 and to confirm. Waiting on reply.

maya: long-term we should offer them one of these options: (1) configure a static reserved egress IP via Dedicated/Private reserved SNAT, (2) use DNS-based allowlisting with our egress-hostname, or (3) use mutual TLS/HTTP auth so IPs don't matter.

samir: agreed. customer replied: "we added 34.125.210.77 and webhooks started flowing again" :thumbsup:

julia: good. they also asked why the IP changed without a heads-up — can we confirm notification flow failed? The maintenance notice was posted but maybe not sent to their workspace.

luis: maintenance note was sent to infra-notifications and via email to org-admins on 2026-03-16 18:00 UTC. I'll double-check the customer contact list for that org.

maya: can we add a small internal followup to automate a customer-facing notice for NAT changes that affect registered webhooks? Maybe an opt-in flag per account for "egress IP change alerts".

samir: created follow-up todo: DOCS-1422 — "egress IP change notif option + recommended webhook configs". tagging product.

luis: also a quick ops note: our rotation script toggles SNATs to evenly spread allocations. We can add a conditional to avoid rotating egress for accounts with flagged webhook endpoints. Will file infra task.

julia: final status for this thread: root cause = NAT egress IP rotated to 34.125.210.77, customer firewall was still only allowing 34.125.201.45; resolution = customer added new IP; follow-ups = DOCS-1422 (docs), INFRA-667 (rotation opt-out). I'll close ticket once customer confirms no further fails.

samir: thanks all — please add any logs to the ticket. marking incident as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
